Commentary.Commentary: That wraps up the formalities of this game. The action now shifts to Hobart where the second Test starts on 12th November. Not much time to reflect for the Australians and they'll have to regroup fast. South Africa will want to seal the series there itself. The action starts at 0500 IST. Do join us for that one. Till then, enjoy our coverage of the ongoing Zimbabwe-Sri Lanka Test and the India-England Test that will start on 9th November. Till then, it's goodbye from us.

Faf du Plessis says that it wasn't easy in the fourth innings with just two pacers. Lauds Rabada and Philander for stepping up in Steyn's absence. States that they were below par on day one and adds that there were some harsh words spoken. Adds that the comeback in the remaining days was unbelievable. Lauds the whole team for putting up a collective effort.

Steven Smith says that it is a disappointing result especially after bossing the first day's play. Bemoans that they couldn't capitalize on the position. Feels that Duminy and Elgar took it away from Australia. Admits that the batting collapses in recent times has hurt his side and hopes that they can sort it out. States that they have to put up an improved show in the next game at Hobart. Praises South Africa for playing great cricket and says that he always enjoys playing for the country.

Kagiso Rabada (Man of the Match) says that he is proud of his team's efforts especially after losing Steyn. Says that the senior pacer's absence hurt but adds that it motivated the others to step up. Feels that the track was mostly flat although there was a little help for the bowlers. Felt that his side executed their plans really well. Says that he'd be ready for the next Test match.

Rabada was the bowling star in the second innings for SA and it won't be wrong to say that he singlehandedly bowled the Proteas to a win especially with Philander not looking as threatening. They lost Steyn midway through the second session on day two but the others ensured that the tourists weren't affected. Philander stepped up in the first innings and Rabada led the charge in the second. AUSTRALIA'S 18-MATCH UNBEATEN STREAK AT HOME HAS BEEN BROKEN.

Duminy and Elgar struck tons to blunt the Aussie bowling which was backed up by the SA lower order. The hosts' bowlers were ground to dust and by the time Faf declared on day 4, the target read a massive 539. Australia's top order had to step up but only Khawaja registered a significant score. Warner and Smith wasted starts to make things worse for the hosts. Having lost four top order wickets by stumps on day 4, the result was never in doubt despite some heroics by the lower order.

The game will be remembered for the stunning comeback made by South Africa after being destroyed on day 1. They posted just 242 and Australia had raced to 105/0 by stumps. It then became 158/0 by drinks on day 2 before the terrible collapse followed. South Africa through Philander's brilliance roared back in style to restrict Australia to just 244. The deficit was just 2 for the tourists and from there on, it was mostly one-way traffic in the match.

A comprehensive win by South Africa although the Aussie lower order did delay the inevitable for a while. The day started with the tourists needing six wickets to win and they got three in the first session itself including the big one of the well-set Khawaja who narrowly missed out on his ton. Nevill and Hazlewood ate out more than 20 overs to frustrate the visitors but Bavuma broke the stubborn stand before Maharaj wrapped things up.

Barring the odd hiccup, Usman Khawaja has looked quite solid on this deteriorating WACA surface. With his spot under scrutiny, the southpaw will have to play a really big knock if the home side are to take this game deep today. Mitchell Marsh too has been under criticism and he will also have to step up. South Africa may be a bowler short but with the spinners getting the ball to grip, I doubt the visitors will be too worried. Let's see how the first session shapes up. The action isn't far away.

Hello and welcome to our coverage of the final day's play. South Africa need another six wickets to complete what would be a decimating victory over the Aussies. Still another 370 runs needed for the hosts and it's safe to say that a victory is out of the equation for them. Can they show grit and determination to save this game? It'll take some doing I tell you, considering that they are already four down and up against a furious Kagiso Rabada and co. The surface is still decent to bat but there's certainly more wear as you'd expect on day five.
.....DAY 5, SESSION 1.....

The pair of Khawaja and Marsh has prevented further damage but the writing is on the wall for Australia. Rabada and Philander bowled superbly for the tourists with the former standing out. Maharaj too caused problems as he got the ball to spin off the cracks. Such has been the effectiveness of the bowling that Steyn's absence hasn't been felt at all. Although a draw cannot be ruled out, the probability of SA sealing a win tomorrow is paramount. Tune in at 0800 IST for the final day's play.

Khawaja and Smith stitched a solid partnership to get the innings back on track before Rabada produced a compelling spell late in the day to strike twice. He first removed Smith and then had Voges in his next over to leave the hosts in a hole. Khawaja continued to battle on and got past his fifty, a knock that featured some smart shots with the occasional streaky stroke.

.....DAY 4, SESSION 3.....

The momentum was completely in the favour of the visitors and they grabbed another one in the name of Shaun Marsh in the same over. Since then, Smith and Khawaja have settled up and seen through the session without further casualty. The Aussies have to take it session by session and their first motto will be to see off the day. If the current pair gets them through, that will bring life back for them. South Africa on the other hand will be looking to continue the good work and build on the momentum. Join us for the final session in a short while.

Another session truly bagged by the Proteas! They are up and running with the game at the moment. After lunch, they crashed-banged-walloped a few to take the lead to 538 before Faf du Plessis declared. Australia had their task cut out and to be frank, Warner and Marsh started off well with sheer onus on the former. He was looking good but a terrific work from the little man, Temba Bavuma in the field spelled the end for the Australian vice captain.
Very full around off, Khawaja digs it out. THAT WILL BE TEA ON DAY 4!
Around middle and leg, Khawaja gets across and defends it on the leg side.
Prods forward and blocks it out safely.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

FOUR BYES! What was that? Loopy ball around off, it hits one of the cracks and dies down. Khawaja looks to drive but is undone by the low bounce as the ball goes past the stumps and through the legs of the keeper for a boundary.
Around middle and off, Khawaja defends it off the front foot.
Angles it on the pads, flicked towards the leg side.
Back of a length ball on middle, Smith gets back and defends it towards the leg side.
FOUR! Too easy for Stevey! Fuller and angling in on the pads, Smith takes full toll of it as he flicks it through square leg and finds the fence.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Good length ball on middle, Smith defends it with a straight bat.
Fuller in length and outside off, Smith defends it towards the off side off the front foot.
Comes forward and defends it down watchfully.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

SIX! Nailed it! What a shot that is, Usman! Maharaj floats it up around off, Khawaj jumps down the track, gets to the pitch of the delivery and hits it inside out over extra cover for a maximum. Terrific!
Low full toss around off, drilled straight to the man at short cover.
FOUR! Delightful! Tossed up delivery around off, Khawaja makes a long stride forward and drives it through extra cover. Beats the chase of the mid off fielder and gets a boundary.
Tossed up delivery around off, UK prods forward and blocks.
Fuller and angling in, Smith presses forward and blocks it out.
That's four in a row for the Aussie skipper. Good length ball on off, Smith doesn't fiddle with it.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Outside off. Steven lets it through.
In the channel outside off, Smith shoulders his arms to that one.
On a length and outside off, Smith defends it with a straight bat.
Flattish on off, defended well.
Leg bye! Worked off the pads towards short fine leg for one.
Around middle and leg, flicked towards the leg side.

Was there bat? Tossed up ball around off, Smith comes down the track to defend but misses as the ball goes off the pads towards silly point where the fielder gives fails to clings onto it. South Africans were excited but that was clearly pads.
Loopy ball around off, defended it down gently.
Flatter one around middle, Smith gets back and flicks it sweetly through mid-wicket for a couple.
On a length and outside off, Usman defends it down gently.
Fuller in length outside off, Khawaja shoulders his arms to that one.
Stands tall in the crease and defends it down gently.
Back of a length delivery on off, Smith punches it towards Bavuma at point and takes him on for a quick single.
Back of a length delivery on off, Khawaj comes forward and defends it towards covers. There is a misfield and a single is on offer.
On a good length and just outside off, Khawaja looks to defend but gets beaten all ends up.
Short and around off, Smith hangs back and punches it down the wicket.
Gets behind the line and defends it down watchfully.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Loopy ball around middle and off, defended gently off the front foot.
Smith comes down the track and blocks it out.
Darted around middle and leg, worked towards the leg side.
Beaten! Full and angling in from outside off, holds its line after pitching as Khawaja is beaten on the poke.
Good length outside off, Khawaja lifts his bat to make the leave.
Short of a length outside off, slapped off the back foot to cover. Bavuma misses the shy at the bowler's end as Smith makes it back.
Good length angled in around off, Khawaja pushes at it but gets an edge towards cover.
Length ball angling away outside off, no shot offered to it.
Good length closer to off, defended well from the crease.
Vernon Philander is back on.
Flighted outside off, defended off the front foot towards silly point.
Flatter on middle and leg, whipped towards Bavuma at short leg. Rebounds towards mid-wicket.
Floated outside off, blocked off the front foot to the covers.
Fuller and outside off, Khawaja drives it to deep mid off for a single.
Mid-wicket drops back to the fence. Not sure why though, as there is a mountain of runs in the tank for the Proteas and that shot was surely risky.
FOUR! Smacked! Drifting in from around off, Khawaja goes across and sweeps it hard through mid-wicket to find the fence. That was hit really hard.
Tossed up outside off, Khawaja presses forward and smothers it to the ground.
Keshav Maharaj comes on to bowl.

FOUR! Targets the stumps but slips a wayward one! Rabada fires it full and down the leg side, Smith looks to flick but misses. de Kock couldn't stop with a dive to his right either as it races down to the fine leg fence. Surprisingly, the umpire doesn't calls it byes. Smith had little bit of wood involved there.
Angles it on middle, Smith covers the line and jams it out.
On a length and outside off, Smith lifts his bat and lets it go.
Outside off, it's been left alone by Smith.
Good length ball on middle, defended from within the crease.
In the channel outside off, Smith shoulders his arms to that one.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Tossed up around off, Khawaja drives it firmly towards mid off.
Full toss around off, Khawaja drives it towards covers. Would be kicking himself to not let that send to the ropes.
Flicked past short leg towards square leg.
Down the leg side, UK looks to flick but misses.

NOT OUT! The decision is overturned! Duminy bowls a loopy ball around off, turning in as well. Khawaja gets back to cut but misses and de Kock behind the stumps grabs it. He immediately goes up in an appeal and umpire Llong rules it out. Usman takes the review and after having a continuous look at the replays, the TV umpire says not out as nothing was seen on Hot Spot nor on Snicko. Khawaja survives and that should calm the nerves in the Australia dressing room.
Usman Khawaja is given out caught behind. South Africa look confident. Khawaja takes the review!
Steven Smith walks in next. He got out on a duck in the first innings, can he redeem himself? He has to, his team needs it badly.

OUT! Edged and gone! Australia have lost both their openers in the span of four balls. Good length delivery on off, Shaun Marsh feels for it and pays the price for the same. Thick outside edge is induced and Faf du Plessis at second slip takes a regulation catch. Australia in big trouble now.
In the channel outside off, Marsh leaves it alone.
On a good length and outside off, Marsh pokes at it and gets an outside edge towards gully where Duminy makes a diving stop to his right.
Fuller in length and outside off, defended off the front foot.
Usman Khawaja is the new man in, replacing Warner!

OUT! RUN OUT! Warner is short of his ground! This is simply outstanding from Temba Bavuma. Australia in a spot of bother now as they have lost a big wicket in the form of David Warner. Length ball on off, Warner taps it towards short cover and calls for a single immediately. Bavuma stationed there quickly gets to the ball, picks it up and flicks a throw at the non-striker's end. All in one motion and much to his delight it hits the timber at that end. Touch and go and the umpire takes it upstairs. Replays show Warner is just short to make it in. South Africa get their first wicket.
Appeal for a run out is being sent upstairs. Good stuff from Bavuma.

FOUR1 Edged and over the third slip fielder! Rabada hurls it on a length outside off, Warner tries to play it away from the body. Gets a thick outside edge which flies over a leaping Dean Elgar at third slip for a boundary. He got out in a similar fashion in the first innings as well.
Loopy ball around middle and off, Marsh looks to flick it across the line but misses and is hit on the pads as the ball goes towards the off side.
Gets back in time and flicks it past short leg. Marsh wanted a single but Warner sends him back in time.
Around off, Warner comes down the track and flicks it towards mid on for an easy single.
Comes down the track and drives it towards mid on for a single.
Loopy ball around off, driven straight to the man at short cover.
Loopy ball around off, Warner plays it off the front foot but gets an inside edge through the legs towards square leg for a single.
Fuller in length on off, Marsh prods forward and defends it towards covers.
Back of a length on off, Marsh sways in time.
Wide! Banged in short on off, too high for the batsman to play at it. The umpire stretches his arms.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Angles it full on the pads, Sm gets across and flicks it towards mid on.
Fires it on off, hits the crack and doesn't rise off the deck. Marsh comfortably plays inside the line and it goes on the bounce to de Kock.
Good length ball on middle, tucked towards the leg side for a single.

With South Africa a bowler short due to Steyn's unavailability, the tourists have had several of their batsmen trying to bowl in the nets over the last two days. Among those, Bavuma and Cook were the main ones who were seen practicing gentle medium pace.

FOUR! Lovely use of the feet! Duminy bowls a loopy full toss around middle, Marsh comes down the track and flicks it beautifully through wide mid on as it races away to the fence for a boundary. Good shot!
Makes a stride forward and defends it back to JP.
Comes forward and defends it down gently.
Tossed up outside off, Marsh still goes after it but gets beaten.
Leg bye! Slides it around middle and leg, Warner comes forward to flick but it bruishes his pads and rolls past short leg. A leg bye is taken.
Tossed up ball around off, Warner drives it hard but straight to the man at short extra cover.
JP Duminy is brought into the attack. A good move from SA. A slip and short leg in place for him.
Angles in a length ball on middle, tucked towards square leg for one.
Fuller in length on off, Warner prods forward and defends it towards covers.
FOUR! Fantastic! Back of a length delivery, width on offer too. Warner doesn't try to play it with hard hands, uses the pace and just steers it through point and earns himself a classy boundary.
Fuller in length on middle, driven towards mid on.

Another full ball on middle and leg, Marsh flicks it past the man at square leg. The fielder gives it a chase and does well to put in a dive. They check it upstairs if he made contact with the rope when he had the ball in his hand. All fine and they get three.
Fuller in length and on middle, worked straight to the man at square leg.
On a length and outside off, nipping back in sharply. Warner comes forward and leaves it alone.
Length ball on off, Warner gets across and defends it down on the track.
Comes back in from outside off, Warner defends it solidly.
Fuller in length and around off, Warner comes on the front foot and drives it towards mid off.
Fuller and angling in, Warner gets across and works it through wide mid on for a double.
Very full on from around the wicket, Warner pushes it back to the bowler who stops it by bending to his right.
Angles it down the leg side, Shaun has got nothing to do with it.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Good length ball on off, Marsh answers it with a straight bat.
Fuller in length on off, Marsh sees it early as he makes up his mind and lets it pass through. de Kock dives full length to his right to stop that one, brilliant!
Fuller in length and curling in sharply. Marsh flicks it past a fumbling short mid-wicket fielder for a brace.
Shortish outside off, Marsh looks to cut this one through the off side but gets a bottom edge towards first slip.
Fullish in length on off, David jams it down towards mid on.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Length ball on off, Marsh wanted to go after it and then does well to pull out the willow at the last moment.
On a length and outside off, punched off the back foot towards extra cover fr a single.
Back of a length ball on middle, Warner gets back and defends it with a straight bat.
Sprays on the pads, Marsh crouches forward and helps this one down to fine leg. Just a single.
Fuller on middle and leg, Warner clips it towards fine leg. Philander fumbles in the deep and that allows them to come back for a double.
Short of a length ball on middle, Warner tucks it towards the leg side.
FOUR! Crunched! Touch full and around the off stump line, Warner leans into it and caresses it through covers again. No need to run for those.
FOUR! Finds the gap, David! Short of a length ball on off, Warner gets back, keeps his head straight and punches it through covers. Splits the gap and Bavuma's chase was never looking good.
Back of a length and outside off, Davey punches it on the up but straight to the man at short extra cover.
Good length delivery on middle and leg, Warner shows some patience and defends it with the full face of the bat.
Back of a length just outside off, Shaun leaves it alone.
Fuller in length and outside off, SM defends it towards the off side nicely.
Fuller in length and outside off, Marsh makes a brave leave to de Kock.
In the channel outside off, Marsh shoulders his arms to that one.
On a good length and outside off, Marsh gets behind the line and taps it towards covers.
On a good length and wide outside off, no harm for SM.
Swoosh! Short of a length ball on off, at 145.5 clicks. Warner looks to slash it hard through point but is beaten by the extra bounce.
Back of a length delivery on middle, Shaun pulls it behind square on the leg side for a single.
Fuller in length and on off, defended off the front foot.
On a length and outside off, Marsh hangs back and offers a straight bat defense.
Good running! Good length ball on middle, worked off the inner part of the bat towards fine leg for a couple.
Short of a length ball on leg, Marsh looks to flick but misses and it hit on the pads.
Short of a length ball on off, defended off the back foot.
Philander is targeting those cracks. Fuller in length and nipping in a shade, Warner flicks it off the inner part towards mid on.
Angles away a length delivery on off, touch full as well. Warner pushes it through covers. Bavuma gives it a chase and keeps them down to a couple.
Good length ball, curling back in, Warner gets back and defends it down.
FOUR! Back-to-back boundaries! On a length and outside off, Warner stays back, uses the pace and steers it behind point to find the fence.

FOUR! Warner is off the mark! My colleague sitting next to me says, be the target 500 or 600, Warner will play his shots! Back of a length and outside off, Warner cuts it through point and Australia are underway.
Vernon Philander will share the new cherry from the other end!
Angles in a length delivery on middle, Marsh looks to flick but gets a leading edge on the pads. A maiden to start the proceedings!
A length ball down the leg side, stays a touch low as well. Shaun gets inside the line to flick but misses. It goes on the bounce to de Kock.
Slants it on a length and outside off, Marsh has got nothing to offer.
On a good length and outside off, Shaun Marsh lifts his bat and lets it through.
Back of a length delivery on off, Marsh hops a bit and pushes it timidly towards point.
Rabada starts off with a length delivery in the channel outside off, Shaun Marsh makes a customary leave.
